name: Block Dominoes
description: Block Dominoes is the foundational Western domino game and the simplest form of line play. Players take turns matching tiles from their hand to one of the two open ends of the central 'train'. If a player cannot move, they must pass—there is no drawing from a boneyard in the block variant. The round ends when someone 'dominoes' (empties their hand) or when the game is blocked. It is a game of simple arithmetic, hand management, and tactical blocking.

overview.description: Block Dominoes is the foundational Western domino game and the simplest form of line play. history.origins: Modern dominoes likely originated in China before being introduced to Europe in the 18th century. Block Dominoes represents the most direct adaptation of card-matching mechanics to tile components and serves as the 'mother game' for nearly all Western variants like Draw and Muggins.
timeline: 12th Century: Earliest references to tiles in Chinese literature.
1700s: Dominoes appear in Italy and France.
1800s: Block Dominoes becomes a standard feature of British and American pub culture.
Present: Remains the most widely played domino game globally.
history.cultural: A staple of social gatherings, particularly in the Caribbean and Latin America, where it is often played with high intensity and speed.
history.evolution: The game has remained virtually unchanged for over two centuries, with its simplicity allowing it to cross language and cultural barriers easily.

setup.players: 2 to 4 players (4 players usually play in fixed partnerships).
setup.deck: Standard double-six domino set consisting of 28 tiles.
setup.dealing: 2 players: 7 tiles each. 3 players: 5 tiles each. 4 players: 5 or 7 tiles each (depending on whether the boneyard is used). Remaining tiles are set aside face down.

rules.objective: Be the first player to play all tiles from your hand, or have the lowest pip count in a blocked game.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Start**: The player with the highest double (usually 6-6) plays first. 2. **Turn**: Each player in turn must place one tile that matches the pip value of an open end of the line. 3. **Doubles**: Doubles are played crosswise but are not spinners; they only provide two matching ends. 4. **Passing**: If you cannot play, you must pass your turn. 5. **End**: The round ends when a player is out of tiles or no player can make a move.
keyRules: The line always has exactly two open ends.
No drawing from the boneyard during play.
In a blocked game, the player with the lowest total pips wins the round.

strategy.basic: Lead with your strongest suit (the number you have the most of). This ensures you have more opportunities to play on the ends you create.
strategy.intermediate: Suit Control: Try to keep your strong suits at both ends of the line. This forces opponents to pass while you continue to shed tiles.
strategy.advanced: Blocking: If you have a hand with low pip counts, you may deliberately block the game if you know opponents have high cards they cannot play. Tracking played tiles is essential to know which suits are exhausted.
tips: Play your doubles as early as possible, as they are the hardest tiles to match late in the game.
Keep a diverse range of suits in your hand to avoid being forced to pass.

variations.name: Draw Dominoes
variations.description: Identical to Block, but players must draw from the boneyard when they cannot move.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Draw Dominoes introduces boneyard drawing, but its engine-level differences are not yet modelled as overrides.

scoring.description: Winner scores sum of losers' pips minus own pips. Game to 100 (2-player/partnership) or 61 (3-4 player).
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach the target score across multiple rounds.

synthesis.shortDescription: The simplest and most common domino game in the world. Match tiles end-to-end on a single train. Can't play? You pass — there's no boneyard draw in Block. First to empty your hand or lowest pips when it blocks wins. The foundation of all Western domino games.
